text: This is Backroom. A client has one point of contact. Behind it, Switch carries the brief, build and review. I decide what leaves.
This bakery is fictional, and the completed rehearsal used simulated owner and client approvals.
Here is a revision. A question keeps the stage open. A change creates a new version and reopens the approvals it affects.
The completed native rehearsal changed the confirmation heading. A separate hand rehearsal changed pickup sessions.
The architecture has its own decision. Asking a question does not approve it. Changing it replaces the approval target.
An old code cannot release the replacement.
Switch carries the handoff into the build and back to review. The rehearsal needed corrections.
The final fresh review accepted the recorded commit, with that review bounded to its stated finding.
The release refers to the reviewed commit. The owner approves delivery, then the client accepts that deployment. The app saves a pre-order.
A health response alone is not proof that the product works.
Plain-code desk checks who approved the frozen content. An agent-authored send was rejected in the earlier test.
The product video has a separate gate: owner approval, delivery, then client acceptance of the exact file.
Memory must change the work. The sample price lesson puts prices on the server.
A later privacy lesson was approved and attached through a Switch package.
It led to a local fix branch for the earlier sample shop. No hosted pull request was opened.
Switch carries the handoffs. I keep the release decisions. This is a local demo, not a strong sandbox.
The receipt shows what was tested and what still needs a real run.
